_comment: Identity policy for the role the AGENT holds. It can read the account and compute a
plan; it cannot mutate anything. Attach alongside the AWS managed policy
arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess -- that is what `terraform plan` needs for its
refresh and its data sources, and this file only adds the narrow state-backend access
on top. Attaching this file ALONE leaves a role that fails on the first Describe call.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID>, <STATE_BUCKET>, <LOCK_TABLE>, and the cross-account read role ARNs.

Statement._comment: plan reads state; it does not write it. PutObject is denied below.

_comment: Read-only on the state CMK. GenerateDataKey is the apply role's, because writing a
new state object needs it and reading an existing one does not.
plan is not purely read-only: with the S3 backend it takes and releases the
DynamoDB lock. Scoped to the lock table alone. Do not solve this with -lock=false;
an unlocked plan against a shared state races an apply.
SCOPED, not denied outright. A hub-and-spoke lakehouse plans across accounts through
aliased providers with assume_role blocks, so a blanket deny on sts:AssumeRole makes
that architecture unplannable. List exactly the read roles; everything else is denied
by the statement below, which is what stops a provider block naming an admin role.
The escalation path this closes: an agent authoring HCL can write
provider "aws" { assume_role { role_arn = "...AdminRole" } }. That only works if
the CALLER may assume it. NotResource, so the two read roles above stay reachable
and every other role -- including the apply role -- does not.
Unconditional, and belt-and-braces over ReadOnlyAccess. ReadOnlyAccess grants no
writes today, but attaching one more policy to this role must not be able to make it
mutating by accident: an explicit Deny cannot be overridden by any Allow.
Not an exhaustive list of every mutating action -- that is unmaintainable and would
be the same fail-open denylist this project rejects elsewhere. It is the subset that
destroys or escalates. The real boundary is that the role holds only ReadOnlyAccess
plus the statements above; this is the second line.
